name: Dexcom

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Dexcom logo.svg; includes the tagline CONTINUOUS GLUCOSE MONITORING)

description: Dexcom makes continuous glucose monitors (CGMs): a small sensor worn on the body that sends blood-sugar readings to a phone or receiver, for people with diabetes and, with Stelo, for people without it. The money is in the disposable sensors, which are replaced every 10 to 15 days and bought again and again; the reusable transmitter or receiver is secondary. Sales go mostly through pharmacies and medical-supply distributors paid by insurers and Medicare, plus a direct sales force. Growth comes from adding customers (about 600,000 to 700,000 net in 2025 excluding Stelo) while price per sensor is pushed down by rebates.

businessLines.how: Recurring disposable sensor sales (sensors last 10 to 15 days) to patients through pharmacy and durable-medical-equipment channels reimbursed by insurers and Medicare; revenue is customers times sensors times net price after rebates.

businessLines.name: International
businessLines.how: Same sensor model sold through direct sales and distributors in several international markets.
